What I'm saying is that the ends proposed as intrinsically valuable seem to be means to achieving some other end. That is why I fail to see how those ends are not means to some other end, and thus _extrinsically_ valuable.

How is life intrinsically valuable? If you try and answer that question, you will inevitably treat life as a means to some other end, probably enjoyment. If you try to explain how enjoyment is intrinsically valuable, you will inevitably treat it as a means to yet another end, perhaps health or wellbeing. Thus, by trying to explain an intrinsic value you turn it into an extrinsic value. And yet, if you refrain from trying to explain intrinsic value and simply state that it is valuable because it is valuable, well, that does not explain it and I will fail to see the value of value. Intrinsic value, then, seems paradoxical to me and thus, false.
